scheme: letter = grid row (A-E top to bottom); number = 1-7 left to right with 4 on the symmetry axis in rows C/D/E (mirror pairs sum to 8), grid-cell number in rows A/B. Suffix when one handwritten label covers several pieces: -L/-R side by side, -T/-M/-B stacked top to bottom on the axis. 'written' is the artist's handwritten label the piece sits under (null when it has none of its own); 'confidence' is low when the label is inferred rather than read. Entries are keyed by centroid (cx, cy) and area in map pixels; assign_labels attaches them to the nearest segmented piece.
notes: Pieces the artist drew touching (shared ink line, no paper gap) segment as one component: the leg assemblies D1 and D7 (crescent + hip blob + foot each). The bottom label strip reads D1 . E3 . E4 . D6 . D7, so the artist seems to count the right foot as D6 (and by symmetry the left foot as D2); those sub-pieces are not separable without cutting along ink.
The small pod C4-M sits on the lozenge C4-B with a gap of a pixel or two; it separates with the default parameters but is the most fragile boundary of the map.
A1, A5 and E1 are empty grid cells; their labels mark no piece.
